module purpose: neorv32_twi is a bus-controlled serial SDA/SCL engine. It stores control settings, queues outgoing 11-bit command/data words into a TX FIFO, generates timed SCL/SDA outputs while sampling incoming SCL/SDA into internal state and an RX FIFO, reports status/data on the bus response, asserts clkgen_en_o when enabled, and raises irq_o when enabled and idle with no pending TX data.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into held fields ctrl.enable, ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.clkstr
a queued command/data word written to the TX FIFO and loaded into the transfer engine when idle and ticked
serial transfer timing, phase sequencing, SDA/SCL drive, and SDA sampling during a transfer
control and live status values returned on control-register reads
received 9-bit result read from the RX path
bus response, enable/timing state, interrupt, clock-generation state, engine state, and SDA/SCL output state forced to known reset values

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes ctrl.enable from bus data at line 136 under the addressed write conditions in lines 133-135, and reset clears it at line 124. Its value directly clears both FIFOs through fifo.clear at line 168, disables clock generation at lines 252-254, re-initializes phase sequencing at lines 280-281, is copied into engine.state at line 321, gates irq_o at line 239, and leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o at line 270. Integrity is established because these implemented enable/disable effects must follow the stored setting; availability is also established because the value is held until overwritten or reset. The bus request/response record ports carry complete transactions, so the stored internal field and the exported scalar output are the eligible structural references here.

The configure flow writes ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.clkstr at lines 137-139. ctrl.prsc selects the incoming clock-generator bit at line 257, ctrl.cdiv is compared with clk_gen.cnt at line 258 to assert clk_gen.tick at line 259, and ctrl.clkstr qualifies the halt condition at line 296. Integrity is established because wrong stored fields change when transfer ticks are generated and whether phase advance pauses. Availability is established because these are held settings used repeatedly by the operate flow. Reset initializes ctrl.prsc and ctrl.cdiv at lines 125-126; this RTL does not assign ctrl.clkstr in the reset arm at lines 122-127, so its established availability is after write rather than reset initialization.

The operate flow computes and stores the decisions that advance or stop a transfer: twi_scl_i is sampled at line 409 and stored in io_con.scl_in_ff at line 315; clk_gen.halt is computed at line 296 and blocks phase advance unless low at line 282; clk_gen.tick is generated in the clock generator at lines 257-259; clk_gen.phase_gen is initialized or rotated at lines 281-283 and phase pulses are derived at lines 289-292; engine.state is updated from ctrl.enable at line 321, from queued command bits at line 329, and back to idle at lines 344, 353, 387, and 394; engine.bitcnt increments at line 382; engine.done is asserted at line 386; engine.busy is computed from engine.state at line 401. These values control TX FIFO pop at line 199, output updates at lines 334-375, RX write at line 229, status generation at line 154, and interrupt qualification at line 239. Integrity is established because the implemented transfer sequence, byte completion, and busy/idle behavior depend on these exact state transitions and decisions; availability is established because the values are held or recomputed on each clock under RTL-visible conditions. The delayed phase register clk_gen.phase_gen_ff at line 279 is an implementation helper carrying the previous phase for the phase-pulse computation and is not listed separately.

conceptual assets.concept: Current transfer byte together with the sampled acknowledge/data bit
conceptual assets.reasoning: In idle engine state, engine.sreg is loaded from the queued TX word at line 327; during transfer, the incoming SDA sample enters the module at line 408, is synchronized into io_con.sda_in_ff at line 314, and is shifted into engine.sreg at line 378. The current transfer bit is taken from engine.sreg for output at line 374, and after completion the value is packed for RX storage at line 228 and written when engine.done is asserted at line 229. Integrity is established because the transmitted bit sequence and captured response byte/ack must follow these assignments; availability is established because engine.sreg and the input sampler retain and update the in-flight value across clock edges until write-out. The RX FIFO internals are not supplied and bus_rsp_o is a transport record, so the eligible in-block references are the sampled-input path and engine.sreg before it is written out.

conceptual assets.concept: Driven serial line levels on SDA and SCL
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow stores and exports the line-drive decisions. io_con.sda_out is updated in the engine at lines 335, 337, 350, 352, 372, 374, and 393; io_con.scl_out is updated at lines 341, 343, 357, 359, 366, 368, and 392. The entity then drives twi_sda_o and twi_scl_o directly from those registers at lines 406-407. Integrity is established because the module's external behavior is defined by these exact driven levels on the serial lines; availability is established because the registers hold the driven value between clock edges and the ports continuously present it.

The report flow computes irq_o on each clock as ctrl.enable and not fifo.tx_avail and not engine.busy at line 239, with reset forcing 0 at line 237. Integrity is established because the consumer of irq_o must receive exactly the implemented event that the interface is enabled but neither busy nor holding pending TX data. Availability is established because irq_o is updated every clock under those RTL-visible conditions.
